title: Sell Mineral Rights in Monticello, UT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Monticello, UT | County Seat
metaDescription: Own mineral rights recorded at the San Juan County courthouse in Monticello, Utah? We buy Paradox Basin interests directly, with title confirmed first.
heroLead: As the San Juan County seat, Monticello is where the paperwork trail for minerals across this wide, geologically varied county ultimately gets filed.
intro: Monticello sits at higher elevation than most of San Juan County, on the edge of the Abajo Mountains, and serves as the administrative center for a county that spans everything from the Cane Creek shale near Moab to the Aneth Field near the Arizona border. Owners with a Monticello mailing address may hold minerals anywhere across that range, and the actual legal description matters far more than the town name on the envelope.
We buy mineral and royalty interests tied to San Juan County directly, confirming your specific location and production history at the county recorder's office before making an offer.

sections.heading: A wide county with varied geology
paragraphs: San Juan County stretches from the Colorado River canyons near Moab in the north to the Navajo Nation boundary in the south, covering multiple distinct geologic settings within a single county government. A Monticello-area mailing address tells us almost nothing about where an interest is actually located until we pull the legal description, so we always start there rather than assuming based on the county seat's location.

sections.heading: County records and title work
paragraphs: Because the San Juan County Recorder's office is based in Monticello, confirming chain of title for any interest in the county ultimately runs through records filed here, regardless of where the actual mineral tract sits. We handle that research directly and will tell you what we find before asking you to make any decision.

sections.heading: Ranching and timber alongside mineral ownership
paragraphs: Monticello sits at higher elevation with more timber and grazing land nearby than the desert country further south, and many families here hold mineral interests as a secondary asset alongside their ranching operations. We treat the mineral estate as a separate matter from any surface agricultural interest, and selling one does not affect the other.

faqs.question: My mailing address is Monticello but I don't know exactly where my minerals are. Can you find out?
faqs.answer: Yes, we pull the legal description from your deed or division order to determine the actual location, which may be far from Monticello itself.

faqs.question: Is there oil and gas production right around Monticello?
faqs.answer: The immediate area sees less activity than the Cane Creek or Aneth trends elsewhere in the county. We check your specific interest before quoting.

faqs.question: Do all San Juan County mineral records run through Monticello?
faqs.answer: Yes, the county recorder's office is based here, so we do our title research through these records regardless of where your specific tract is located.

faqs.question: Will selling my mineral interest affect our ranching operation?
faqs.answer: No, the mineral estate is a separate asset from surface ranching or grazing land, and a sale does not affect your ranching operation.
